purpose: Test the source-derived metabolic accounting link between compensatory recruitment and insurgent capital depletion on the already-running fresh 24-seed confirmation block.

source_identity.derivation: 0.08 * 30 * 0.8 = 1.92. Recruitment adds fighter-equivalent manpower and converts insurgent capital into supply reserve up to the required reserve level.

fresh_predictions: Across 24 paired fresh worlds, treatment-minus-baseline cumulative recruitment and treatment-minus-baseline canonical insurgent capital are negatively correlated at day 240 with Pearson r <= -0.95.
The same correlation at day 360 is <= -0.95.
The mean capital effect among day-360 rebound worlds is negative.
The mean capital effect among rebound worlds is more negative than among worlds that remain suppressed.

A first-order predicted capital effect of -1.92 * excess recruited mass explains most paired capital variation; report residuals rather than forcing exact equality because reserve saturation, capital constraints, logistics, and other endogenous flows can alter realized cost.
interpretation_rules: Passing the correlation predictions supports a resource-accounting pathway from replacement flow to capital depletion.
Passing the rebound-group predictions supports a regeneration-versus-runway tradeoff: worlds that replace disruption successfully do so at a greater capital cost.
This does not imply a real insurgent organization has the same fighter conversion or supply-cost coefficients.
